note: Hypotheses until validated with customers. No market size, willingness to pay or savings is claimed; consequence_quantified is null by design. Evidence strength 'weak' means search-snippet or inference only; no publisher page was read for those items (sandbox network blocked).

problems.title: Generation-queue statistics mistaken for load-connection timelines
problems.description: Investors and developers may read generation interconnection queue completion/duration as the wait for a data-centre load connection. The two processes are different.
problems.decision_blocked: Whether a campus MW commitment and power date is defensible
problems.consequence: Capital and land committed against a power date the evidence does not support

statements.text: Registry rule 6 and scenario GF-002 already forbid presenting queue stats as load-connection probabilities.
LBNL Queued Up covers generation and storage requests, per the registry entry; not load.
The product's grid-wait assumption can be misread as queue-derived.

unknown: Whether any large-load queue dataset is public per utility
problems.potential_gridforge_solution: Show observed queue history beside the product's assumption, labelled context only (context_bridge exists)
problems.success_metric: Share of reports where queue context is labelled non-load
problems.acceptance_criteria: Product never states a load-connection probability from queue stats

problems.title: Firm versus non-firm or curtailable grid capacity hidden in a single grid-wait number
problems.description: A connection may be offered as non-firm or conditional on on-site generation/storage, which changes the usable capacity and the bridge-power need.
problems.decision_blocked: Whether to rely on grid capacity or size bridge power
problems.consequence: Under-sized bridge power or overstated usable MW

statements.text: Search summaries of law-firm commentary describe CRU Ireland large-energy-user connection policy with dispatchable on-site generation requirements; no CRU page was read.
Product may model contracted power without a firm/non-firm flag.

unknown: Exact CRU decision text and thresholds
problems.potential_gridforge_solution: Independent oracle: contracted vs firm supply; flag when firm capacity is unspecified
problems.success_metric: Share of reports stating firm vs contracted explicitly
problems.acceptance_criteria: A dated result is never produced from contracted MW alone without a firm-capacity statement

problems.title: Large-load process change while a request is pending
problems.description: ERCOT batch study, FERC large-load rulemaking and state tariffs are changing; a timeline can go stale.
problems.decision_blocked: Whether a pending request keeps its timeline
problems.consequence: Stale schedule on a live project

statements.text: Search summaries mention an ERCOT Batch Zero framework and FERC docket RM26-4; neither publisher page was read and status is unverified.

problems.potential_gridforge_solution: Dated evidence records with an as-of date and expiry
problems.success_metric: Share of evidence items carrying as-of dates
problems.acceptance_criteria: Every regulatory input carries a retrieval date and is flagged when stale

problems.title: Transformer and other long-lead equipment critical path missing from schedule
problems.description: Large power transformers have multi-year lead times in public reports; a power date that ignores equipment arrival is unachievable.
problems.decision_blocked: Whether an energisation date can be met
problems.consequence: Energisation date earlier than equipment can arrive

statements.text: The harness workflow already checks that a missing transformer lead time is not silently dated.
Search summaries attribute a ~128-week average power-transformer lead time to Wood Mackenzie (Q2 2025); the page was not read and the full report is paywalled.

unknown: Switchgear/UPS/cooling lead times (no public data found)
problems.potential_gridforge_solution: Independent critical-path oracle recomputed from intake lead times
problems.acceptance_criteria: Date range is never shorter than the longest supplied lead time; missing lead time yields no date

problems.title: Slot reservations and market estimates read as delivery commitments
problems.description: OEM disclosures distinguish firm backlog from slot reservations; a dated market estimate is not a supplier quote.
problems.decision_blocked: Whether bridge power can be delivered by a date
problems.consequence: False confidence in a bridge-power option

statements.text: A search summary of a GE Vernova 8-K reports firm backlog and slot reservations separately; the filing was not read.

problems.potential_gridforge_solution: Evidence classes that separate quote, disclosure, estimate
problems.success_metric: Evidence class stated per lead-time input
problems.acceptance_criteria: No output presents an estimate as a quote

problems.title: MW versus MVA and power-factor slips in grid capacity statements
problems.description: Utility capacity quoted in MVA is mistaken for MW, overstating usable power.
problems.decision_blocked: How many racks a connection supports

statements.text: Harness already tests a power-factor case; audit found no dedicated MVA-vs-MW oracle in workflow.py.

problems.potential_gridforge_solution: Independent supply ceiling min(MVA*pf, contracted MW) - peak
problems.acceptance_criteria: Racks never exceed the intake-derived ceiling

problems.title: BESS power versus energy and duration conflated
problems.description: A BESS rated in MW is credited as firm capacity without checking MWh against required ride-through hours.
problems.decision_blocked: How much firm capacity a BESS provides

statements.text: Audit found no BESS energy-vs-power oracle; product behaviour untested.

problems.potential_gridforge_solution: Oracle: firm credit <= min(MW, MWh / hours)
problems.success_metric: Credit bound holds under MWh cuts
problems.acceptance_criteria: Reducing MWh never increases credited capacity

problems.title: Malformed intake crashes document routes instead of being refused
problems.description: A non-object intake.project escapes as an internal error on deck, proposal, spec and bids, so a customer gets a server error and no deliverable.
problems.decision_blocked: Whether a malformed intake is refused safely
problems.consequence: Unhandled server faults on paid deliverable routes

statements.text: Reproduced 2026-10-30 at product 8bbcdf7: 22 malformed project shapes fault on each of deck, proposal, spec, bids (88 faults).

unknown: Whether HTTP layer converts these to 500
problems.acceptance_criteria: All shapes refused safely; valid examples unchanged
